subject.title: Timeout compaction can report success but leave Codex channel session unrecoverable

question: When repeated Codex timeout compactions still leave a channel session timing out, should OpenClaw automatically reset or roll over the affected session, or only surface explicit manual recovery guidance?
rationale: The fix changes persistent channel-session recovery behavior and may detach active Codex app-server state, so the threshold and side-effect policy need maintainer intent.

options.title: Add guarded auto-rollover
options.body: After bounded repeated timeout compactions, roll over only the affected channel session when no unsafe side effects are active and report the recovery clearly.

options.title: Manual recovery only
options.body: Keep session state intact and surface a precise user/operator message telling them to reset or run the documented recovery flow.

options.title: Defer to broader Codex recovery
options.body: Keep this open until a larger Codex app-server completion and compaction recovery design owns all adjacent timeout cases.

recommendation.title: Add guarded auto-rollover
recommendation.body: After bounded repeated timeout compactions, roll over only the affected channel session when no unsafe side effects are active and report the recovery clearly.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent Codex app-server completion-stall recovery work is the closest already-merged policy surface for retry versus unsafe recovery.
